EX-99.1 2 a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm EX-99.1 October 28, 2026 Constellium Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Results; Raises Full Year 2026 Guidance Paris - Constellium SE (NYSE: CSTM) ("Constellium" or the "Company") today reported results for the third quarter and the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Third quarter 2026 highlights: • Shipments of 368 thousand metric tons, down 1% compared to Q3 2025 • Revenue of $2.6 billion, up 22% compared to Q3 2025 • Net income of $119 million compared to net income of $88 million in Q3 2025 • Adjusted EBITDA of $276 million > Includes negative non-cash metal price lag impact of $4 million • Segment Adjusted EBITDA of $102 million at A&T, $162 million at P&ARP and $21 million at AS&I, partially offset by corporate costs of $(5) million, together representing a new third quarter record for the Company • Cash from Operations of $186 million and Free Cash Flow of $128 million • Returned $30 million to shareholders through the share repurchase program Nine months ended September 30, 2026 highlights: • Shipments of 1.1 million metric tons, down 1% compared to YTD 2025 • Revenue of $7.8 billion, up 26% compared to YTD 2025 • Net income of $463 million compared to net income of $162 million in YTD 2025 • Adjusted EBITDA of $1.1 billion > Includes positive non-cash metal price lag impact of $222 million • Segment Adjusted EBITDA of $340 million at A&T, $478 million at P&ARP and $71 million at AS&I, partially offset by corporate costs of $(37) million, together representing a record first nine months for the Company • Cash from Operations of $420 million and Free Cash Flow of $223 million • Returned $78 million to shareholders through the share repurchase program • Leverage of 1.6x at September 30, 2026 Media Contacts Investor Relations Communications Jason Hershiser Delphine Dahan-Kocher Phone: +1 443 988-0600 Phone: +1 443 420 7860 investor-relations@constellium.com delphine.dahan-kocher@constellium.com 1

“Constellium delivered another strong quarter, including record third quarter Adjusted EBITDA, despite the ongoing uncertainties on the macroeconomic and geopolitical fronts,” said Ingrid Joerg, Constellium’s Chief Executive Officer. “We achieved strong financial performance across all of our operating segments again this quarter, including record third quarter Segment Adjusted EBITDA at both our A&T and P&ARP segments. During the quarter, we benefited from strong operational focus, cost control and improved market dynamics, including an improved aerospace and transportation, industry and defense (TID) environment, supply shortages of automotive rolled products in North America, and strong recycling performance in both North America and Europe. We generated Free Cash Flow of $128 million in the third quarter, and during the quarter we returned $30 million to shareholders through the repurchase of 1.0 million ordinary shares. As a reminder, in July we completed a $100 million partial redemption of the 5.625% Senior Notes due June 2028. We ended the quarter with leverage at 1.6x, near the low end of our target leverage range of 1.5x to 2.5x.” Ms. Joerg continued, "Even though the current landscape remains volatile, we have a strong track record of navigating and executing in any environment. Based on our current outlook, we are raising our guidance for 2026 and now expect Adjusted EBITDA in the range of $1.03 billion to $1.06 billion, excluding the non-cash impact of metal price lag, and Free Cash Flow in excess of $300 million. Looking ahead, we like our end market position and we are optimistic about our prospects, which include harvesting the benefits from our previously announced return-seeking investments and capturing future market opportunities. Our focus remains on executing our strategy, driving operational performance, controlling cost, maintaining commercial and capital discipline, generating Free Cash Flow and increasing shareholder value.” 2

The difference between the sum of reported segment revenue and total group revenue includes revenue from certain non-core activities and inter-segment eliminations. The difference between the sum of reported Segment Adjusted EBITDA and the Group Adjusted EBITDA is related to Holdings and Corporate and the non-cash impact of metal price lag. For the third quarter of 2026, the Company had shipments of 368 thousand metric tons, a decrease of 1% compared to the third quarter of 2025 due to lower shipments in the P&ARP and AS&I segments, partially offset by higher shipments in the A&T segment. Revenue was $2.6 billion, an increase of 22% compared to the third quarter of 2025 due to higher revenue per ton, including higher metal prices, partially offset by lower shipments. Net income of $119 million reflected an increase of $31 million compared to net income of $88 million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $276 million, an increase of $41 million compared to Adjusted EBITDA of $235 million in the third quarter of 2025 due to stronger results in our A&T and P&ARP segments and lower corporate costs, partially offset by weaker results in our AS&I segment, an unfavorable change in the non-cash metal price lag impact, and unfavorable foreign exchange translation. For the first nine months of 2026, the Company had shipments of 1.1 million metric tons, a decrease of 1% compared to the first nine months of 2025 due to lower shipments in the P&ARP and AS&I segments, partially offset by higher shipments in the A&T segment. Revenue was $7.8 billion, an increase of 26% compared to the first nine months of 2025 due to higher revenue per ton, including higher metal prices, partially offset by lower shipments. Net income of $463 million reflected an increase of $301 million compared to net income of $162 million in the first nine months of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.1 billion, an increase of $508 million compared to the first nine months of 2025 due to stronger results in each of our operating segments, a favorable change in the non-cash metal price lag impact, and favorable foreign exchange translation, partially offset by higher corporate costs. 3

Reconciling items excluded from our Segment Adjusted EBITDA include the following: Metal price lag Metal price lag represents the financial impact of the timing difference between when aluminum prices included within Constellium's Revenue are established and when aluminum purchase prices included in Cost of sales are established, which is a non-cash financial impact. The calculation of metal price lag adjustment is based on a standardized methodology applied at each of Constellium’s manufacturing sites. Metal price lag is calculated as the average value of product purchased in the period, approximated at the market price, less the value of product in inventory at the weighted average of metal purchased over time, multiplied by the quantity sold in the period. For the third quarter of 2026, metal price lag was negative, which reflects prices for primary aluminum decreasing during the period. For the third quarter of 2025 and the first nine months of both 2026 and 2025, metal price lag was positive, which reflects prices for primary aluminum increasing during the periods. Other adjustments are detailed in the Reconciliation of net income to Adjusted EBITDA Table on page 16. 6

Net Income For the third quarter of 2026, net income of $119 million compares to net income of $88 million in the third quarter of the prior year. The increase in net income is primarily related to higher gross profit (revenue less cost of sales, excluding depreciation and amortization), partially offset by unfavorable changes in other gains and losses. For the first nine months of 2026, net income of $463 million compares to net income of $162 million in the first nine months of the prior year. The increase in net income is primarily related to higher gross profit (revenue less cost of sales, excluding depreciation and amortization) and favorable changes in other gains and losses, partially offset by higher selling and administrative expenses and higher income tax expense. Cash Flow Cash flows from operating activities were $420 million for the first nine months of 2026 compared to cash flows from operating activities of $271 million in the first nine months of the prior year. Free Cash Flow was $223 million in the first nine months of 2026 compared to $68 million in the first nine months of the prior year. The increase in Free Cash Flow was primarily due to higher Segment Adjusted EBITDA, partially offset by an unfavorable change in working capital. Cash flows used in investing activities were $195 million for the first nine months of 2026 compared to cash flows used in investing activities of $200 million in the first nine months of the prior year. Cash flows used in financing activities were $184 million for the first nine months of 2026 compared to cash flows used in financing activities of $103 million in the first nine months of the prior year. During the first nine months of 2026, the Company repurchased 2.8 million ordinary shares of the Company for $78 million and redeemed $100 million out of the $325 million outstanding aggregate principal amount of its 5.625% Senior Notes due June 2028. During the first nine months of 2025, the Company repurchased 6.5 million ordinary shares of the Company for $75 million. Liquidity and Net Debt Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was $992 million, comprised of $158 million of cash and cash equivalents and $834 million available under our committed lending facilities and factoring arrangements. Total debt was $1,817 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $1,944 million at December 31, 2025. Net debt was $1,658 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $1,824 million at December 31, 2025. As a reminder, in July the Company completed a $100 million partial redemption of the 5.625% Senior Notes due June 2028, leaving $225 million aggregate principal amount outstanding. 7

Outlook Based on our current outlook, we are raising our guidance for 2026 and now expect Adjusted EBITDA in the range of $1.03 billion to $1.06 billion, excluding the non-cash impact of metal price lag, and Free Cash Flow in excess of $300 million. We are not able to provide a reconciliation of this Adjusted EBITDA guidance to net income, the comparable GAAP measure, because certain items that are excluded from Adjusted EBITDA cannot be reasonably predicted or are not in our control. In particular, we are unable to forecast the timing or magnitude of realized and unrealized gains and losses on derivative instruments, metal price lag, impairment or restructuring charges, or taxes without unreasonable efforts, and these items could significantly impact, either individually or in the aggregate, net income in the future. Recent Developments On October 22, 2026, the Pan-U.S. ABL was amended to, among other things, increase the available commitments from $550 million to $700 million and extend the maturity to October 22, 2031. 8

About Constellium Constellium (NYSE: CSTM) is a global sector leader that develops innovative, value-added aluminum products for a broad scope of markets and applications, including aerospace, packaging and automotive. Constellium generated $8.4 billion of revenue in 2025. Constellium’s earnings materials for the third quarter
and the nine months ended September 30, 2026 are also available on the company’s website (www.constellium.com). 9

Non-GAAP measures In addition to the results reported in accordance with United States Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (“U.S. GAAP”), this press release includes information regarding certain financial measures which are not prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP (“non-GAAP measures”). The non-GAAP measures used in this press release are: Adjusted EBITDA, Free Cash Flow and Net debt. Reconciliations to the most directly comparable U.S. GAAP financial measures are presented in the schedules to this press release. We believe these non-GAAP measures are important supplemental measures of our operating and financial performance. By providing these measures, together with the reconciliations, we believe we are enhancing investors’ understanding of our business, our results of operations and our financial position, as well as assisting investors in evaluating the extent to which we are executing our strategic initiatives. However, these non-GAAP financial measures supplement our U.S. GAAP disclosures and should not be considered an alternative to the U.S. GAAP measures and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies. Adjusted EBITDA is not a presentation made in accordance with U.S. GAAP, is not a measure of financial condition, liquidity or profitability and should not be considered as an alternative to profit or loss for the period, revenues or operating cash flows determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The most directly comparable U.S. GAAP measure to Adjusted EBITDA is our net income or loss for the relevant period. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as income / (loss) from continuing operations before income taxes, results from joint ventures, net finance costs, other expenses and depreciation and amortization as adjusted to exclude restructuring costs, impairment charges, unrealized gains or losses on derivatives and on foreign exchange differences on transactions which do not qualify for hedge accounting, share based compensation expense, non-operating gains / (losses) on pension and other post-employment benefits, factoring expenses, effects of certain purchase accounting adjustments, start-up and development costs or acquisition, integration and separation costs, certain incremental costs and other exceptional, unusual or generally non-recurring items. We believe Adjusted EBITDA is useful to investors as it illustrates the underlying performance of continuing operations by excluding certain non-recurring and non-operating items. We believe that Adjusted EBITDA is frequently used by securities analysts, investors and other stakeholders in their evaluation of the Company’s performance. Free Cash Flow is defined as net cash flow from operating activities, less capital expenditures, net of property, plant and equipment inflows. Management believes that Free Cash Flow is a useful measure of the net cash flow generated or used by the business as it takes into account both the cash generated or consumed by operating

activities, including working capital, and the capital expenditure requirements of the business. However, Free Cash Flow is not a presentation made in accordance with U.S. GAAP and should not be considered as an alternative to operating cash flows determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Free Cash Flow has certain inherent limitations, including the fact that it does not represent residual cash flows available for discretionary spending, notably because it does not reflect principal repayments required in connection with our debt or capital lease obligations. 10
Net debt is defined as debt plus or minus the fair value of cross currency basis swaps net of margin calls less cash and cash equivalents and cash pledged for the issuance of guarantees. Management believes that Net debt is a useful measure of indebtedness because it takes into account the cash and cash equivalent balances held by the Company as well as the total external debt of the Company. Net debt is not a presentation made in accordance with U.S. GAAP and should not be considered as an alternative to debt determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Leverage is defined as Net debt divided by last twelve months Segment Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes the non-cash impact of metal price lag. 11
